sanskrit: vānaprasthajanasyāpi darśanaṃ kulavāsinaḥ nāpriyāṇy ācariṣyāmi kiṃ punar grāmavāsinām
english: Even toward the forest-dwelling hermit who keeps to his lineage I shall do no unkindness when he comes into my sight; how much less, then, toward those who dwell in villages.

sanskrit: ekāntaśīlī vimṛśan pakvāpakvena vartayan pitṝn devāṃś ca vanyena vāgbhir adbhiś ca tarpayan
english: Devoted to solitude and given to reflection, I shall sustain myself on what is ripe or unripe, and gratify the ancestors and the gods with the produce of the wild, with sacred words, and with water.

sanskrit: evam āraṇyaśāstrāṇām ugram ugrataraṃ vidhim sevamānaḥ pratīkṣiṣye dehasyāsya samāpanam
english: Thus observing the severe—nay, the ever more severe—ordinance of the forest scriptures, I shall await the ending of this body.

sanskrit: atha vaiko 'ham ekāham ekaikasmin vanaspatau caran bhaikṣyaṃ munir muṇḍaḥ kṣapayiṣye kalevaram
english: Or else, alone and for a single day at the foot of each several tree, a shaven sage going about for alms, I shall wear away this frame.

sanskrit: pāṃsubhiḥ samavacchannaḥ śūnyāgārapratiśrayaḥ vṛkṣamūlaniketo vā tyaktasarvapriyāpriyaḥ
english: Covered over with dust, taking shelter in an empty house, or making my dwelling at the root of a tree, having renounced all that is dear and all that is hateful;

sanskrit: na śocan na prahṛṣyaṃś ca tulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā nirdvaṃdvo niṣparigrahaḥ
english: neither grieving nor rejoicing, holding blame and self-praise alike, having become free of longing, free of possessiveness, beyond the pairs of opposites, and owning nothing;

sanskrit: ātmārāmaḥ prasannātmā jaḍāndhabadhirākṛtiḥ akurvāṇaḥ paraiḥ kāṃ cit saṃvidaṃ jātu kena cit
english: taking delight in the Self, serene of spirit, in semblance like one dull, blind, and deaf, never forming any compact with another, with anyone at all;

sanskrit: jaṅgamājaṅgamān sarvān navihiṃsaṃś caturvidhān prajāḥ sarvāḥ svadharmasthāḥ samaḥ prāṇabhṛtaḥ prati
english: doing no harm to any of the four kinds of beings, moving and unmoving, but even-minded toward all creatures, who abide each in its own nature, toward every bearer of life;

sanskrit: na cāpy avahasan kaṃ cin na kurvan bhrukuṭīṃ kva cit prasannavadano nityaṃ sarvendriyasusaṃyataḥ
english: mocking no one, never knitting the brow in anger anywhere, ever serene of countenance, with all the senses well restrained;

sanskrit: apṛcchan kasya cin mārgaṃ vrajan yenaiva kena cit na deśaṃ na diśaṃ kāṃ cid gantum icchan viśeṣataḥ
english: asking no one the way, walking by whatever path it may be, desiring to go to no particular region and to no particular quarter;

sanskrit: gamane nirapekṣaś ca paścād anavalokayan ṛjuḥ praṇihito gacchaṃs trasasthāvaravarjakaḥ
english: indifferent as to my going, and never looking back behind me, walking straight onward with collected mind, sparing both the moving and the unmoving;

sanskrit: svabhāvas tu prayāty agre prabhavanty aśanāny api dvaṃdvāni ca viruddhāni tāni sarvāṇy acintayan
english: my own nature leading the way before me, my morsels of food springing up of themselves—giving no thought to all those contraries and opposing pairs;

sanskrit: alpaṃ vāsvādu vā bhojyaṃ pūrvālābhena jātu cit anyeṣv api caraṃl lābham alābhe sapta pūrayan
english: food little or savorless, or, when a first round has yielded nothing, going on to other houses too for a gift; and failing of a gift, completing seven such rounds.

sanskrit: vidhūme nyastamusale vyaṅgāre bhuktavaj jane atītapātrasaṃcāre kāle vigatabhikṣuke
english: When the smoke has died, the pestle is laid by, the embers are cold, and the household has eaten, when the passing round of the begging-bowls is over and the hour of mendicants is gone;

sanskrit: ekakālaṃ caran bhaikṣyaṃ gṛhe dve caiva pañca ca spṛhāpāśān vimucyāhaṃ cariṣyāmi mahīm imām
english: going for alms but once a day, to two houses, or to five, freed of the snares of craving, I shall wander over this earth.

sanskrit: na jijīviṣuvat kiṃ cin na mumūrṣuvad ācaran jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ caiva nābhinandan na ca dviṣan
english: Acting in no way as one who longs to live, nor as one who longs to die, neither welcoming life and death nor loathing them;

sanskrit: vāsyaikaṃ takṣato bāhuṃ candanenaikam ukṣataḥ nākalyāṇaṃ na kalyāṇaṃ cintayann ubhayos tayoḥ
english: toward the one who hews my arm with an adze and the one who anoints the other arm with sandal-paste, thinking neither ill nor good of either of the two;

sanskrit: yāḥ kāś cij jīvatā śakyāḥ kartum abhyudayakriyāḥ sarvās tāḥ samabhityajya nimeṣādivyavasthitaḥ
english: having wholly abandoned all those acts of worldly advancement that a living man may perform, abiding within the span of a single instant and the like;

sanskrit: teṣu nityam asaktaś ca tyaktasarvendriyakriyaḥ suparityaktasaṃkalpaḥ sunirṇiktātmakalmaṣaḥ
english: ever unattached to those acts, having forsaken all the workings of the senses, having well renounced all design, having cleansed away the defilement of the self;

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ sarvasaṅgebhyo vyatītaḥ sarvavāgurāḥ na vaśe kasya cit tiṣṭhan sadharmā mātariśvanaḥ
english: released from every clinging, gone beyond all snares, standing in no one's power, sharing the nature of the wind that moves through the sky.

sanskrit: vītarāgaś carann evaṃ tuṣṭiṃ prāpsyāmi śāśvatīm tṛṣṇayā hi mahat pāpaṃ ajñānād asmi kāritaḥ
english: Wandering thus, free of passion, I shall attain to lasting contentment; for it is by craving, out of ignorance, that I have been made to commit great sin.

sanskrit: kuśalākuśalāny eke kṛtvā karmāṇi mānavāḥ kāryakāraṇasaṃśliṣṭaṃ svajanaṃ nāma bibhrati
english: Having done deeds both good and evil, certain men maintain what they call their own kindred, bound together as effect with cause.

sanskrit: āyuṣo 'nte prahāyedaṃ kṣīṇaprāyaṃ kalevaram pratigṛhṇāti tat pāpaṃ kartuḥ karmaphalaṃ hi tat
english: At life's end, when he casts off this all-but-wasted body, that sin lays hold of its doer; for it is the fruit of the deed that belongs to him who did it.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃsāracakre 'smin vyāviddhe rathacakravat sameti bhūtagrāmo 'yaṃ bhūtagrāmeṇa kāryavān
english: Thus, in this wheel of transmigration whirling round like a chariot-wheel, this throng of beings, driven by its tasks, comes together with another throng of beings.

sanskrit: janmamṛtyujarāvyādhivedanābhir upadrutam asāram imam asvantaṃ saṃsāraṃ tyajataḥ sukham
english: For him who forsakes this round of rebirth—pithless and ill-ending, beset by birth, death, old age, sickness, and pain—there is happiness.

sanskrit: divaḥ patatsu deveṣu sthānebhyaś ca maharṣiṣu ko hi nāma bhavenārthī bhavet kāraṇatattvavit
english: When even gods fall from heaven and great seers from their stations, who indeed that knows the truth of causes would still be a seeker after worldly existence?

sanskrit: kṛtvā hi vividhaṃ karma tat tad vividhalakṣaṇam pārthivair nṛpatiḥ svalpaiḥ kāraṇair eva badhyate
english: For having done manifold deeds, each marked by its own diverse character, a king is bound fast by other princes upon the slenderest of pretexts.

sanskrit: tasmāt prajñāmṛtam idaṃ cirān māṃ pratyupasthitam tat prāpya prārthaye sthānam avyayaṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvam
english: Therefore, this nectar of wisdom has at long last come to me; and having gained it, I seek that state which is imperishable, eternal, and fixed.

sanskrit: etayā satataṃ vṛttyā carann evaṃprakārayā dehaṃ saṃsthāpayiṣyāmi nirbhayaṃ mārgam āsthitaḥ
english: Wandering ever by this manner of life, in this very fashion, I shall sustain my body, having set foot upon the path that is free of fear.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca śrotriyasyeva te rājan mandakasyāvipaścitaḥ anuvākahatābuddhir naiṣā tattvārthadarśinī
english: Bhīma said: Like that of some dull, unlettered reciter of scripture, O king, your understanding is deadened by recitations and does not perceive the true meaning of things.

sanskrit: ālasye kṛtacittasya rājadharmānasūyataḥ vināśe dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ kiṃ phalaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: You who have set your heart upon idleness and who spurn the duty of kings—in the destruction of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, what fruit will there be, O bull of the Bharatas?

sanskrit: kṣamānukampā kāruṇyam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ na vidyate kṣātram ācarato mārgam api bandhos tvadantare
english: For one who treads the warrior's path, no forbearance, pity, compassion, or gentleness toward a kinsman has any place in the moment between you and him.

sanskrit: yadīmāṃ bhavato buddhiṃ vidyāma vayam īdṛśīm śastraṃ naiva grahīṣyāmo na vadhiṣyāma kaṃ cana
english: Had we known this mind of yours to be of such a sort, we would never have taken up the weapon, nor would we have slain any man at all.

sanskrit: bhaikṣyam evācariṣyāma śarīrasyā vimokṣaṇāt na cedaṃ dāruṇaṃ yuddham abhaviṣyan mahīkṣitām
english: We would have gone about for alms until the release of the body, and this terrible war of the kings of the earth would never have come to be.

sanskrit: prāṇasyānnam idaṃ sarvam iti vai kavayo viduḥ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva sarvaṃ prāṇasya bhojanam
english: All this is the food of life—so the wise have known; the unmoving and the moving alike, all of it is the nourishment of the breath of life.

sanskrit: ādadānasya ced rājyaṃ ye ke cit paripanthinaḥ hantavyās ta iti prājñāḥ kṣatradharmavido viduḥ
english: Whoever stand in the way of one who is taking a kingdom—those, the wise who know the duty of warriors have declared, must be slain.

sanskrit: te sadoṣā hatāsmābhī rājyasya paripanthinaḥ tān hatvā bhuṅkṣva dharmeṇa yudhiṣṭhira mahīm imām
english: Those guilty men, the obstructers of your kingdom, have been slain by us; having slain them, enjoy this earth in righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yathā hi puruṣaḥ khātvā kūpam aprāpya codakam paṅkadigdho nivarteta karmedaṃ nas tathopamam
english: As a man, having dug a well but reached no water, should turn back smeared with mud—just like that is this work of ours.

sanskrit: yathāruhya mahāvṛkṣam apahṛtya tato madhu aprāśya nidhanaṃ gacchet karmedaṃ nas tathopamam
english: As one, having climbed a great tree and taken the honey from it, should go to his death without tasting it—just like that is this work of ours.

sanskrit: yathā mahāntam adhvānam āśayā puruṣaḥ patan sa nirāśo nivarteta karmedaṃ nas tathopamam
english: As a man, falling along a long road in hope, should turn back hopeless—just like that is this work of ours.

sanskrit: yathā śatrūn ghātayitvā puruṣaḥ kurusattama ātmānaṃ ghātayet paścāt karmedaṃ nas tathāvidham
english: As a man, O best of the Kurus, having had his enemies slain, should afterward destroy himself—of just such a kind is this work of ours.

sanskrit: yathānnaṃ kṣudhito labdhvā na bhuñjīta yadṛcchayā kāmī ca kāminīṃ labdhvā karmedaṃ nas tathāvidham
english: As a hungry man, having got food, should by some whim not eat it, or a lover, having won the woman he desires, should let her go—of just such a kind is this work of ours.

sanskrit: vayam evātra garhyā hi ye vayaṃ mandacetasaḥ tvāṃ rājann anugacchāmo jyeṣṭho 'yam iti bhārata
english: We ourselves are the ones to be blamed in this, we who are dull of wit and who follow you, O king, merely because you are the eldest, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi bāhubalinaḥ kṛtavidyā manasvinaḥ klībasya vākye tiṣṭhāmo yathaivāśaktayas tathā
english: For we, mighty of arm, accomplished in learning, and high of spirit, stand obedient to the word of a weakling, as though we were powerless ourselves.

sanskrit: agatīn kāgatīn asmān naṣṭārthān arthasiddhaye kathaṃ vai nānupaśyeyur janāḥ paśyanti yādṛśam
english: Bereft of all recourse, our purpose ruined just when our aim was to be fulfilled—how should men not look upon us as such men are looked upon?

sanskrit: āpatkāle hi saṃnyāsaḥ kartavya iti śiṣyate jarayābhiparītena śatrubhir vyaṃsitena ca
english: It is taught that renunciation is to be undertaken in a time of calamity—by one overtaken by old age, or one outwitted and undone by his foes.

sanskrit: tasmād iha kṛtaprajñās tyāgaṃ na paricakṣate dharmavyatikramaṃ cedaṃ manyante sūkṣmadarśinaḥ
english: Therefore those of ripened wisdom do not commend renunciation here and now; the keen-sighted hold this very thing to be a transgression of dharma.

sanskrit: kathaṃ tasmāt samutpannas tanniṣṭhas tad upāśrayaḥ tad eva nindann āsīta śraddhā vānyatra gṛhyate
english: How should one who is sprung from it, founded upon it, and sheltered by it, sit there reviling that very thing? Or is one's trust to be placed elsewhere?

sanskrit: śriyā vihīnair adhanair nāstikaiḥ saṃpravartitam vedavādasya vijñānaṃ satyābhāsam ivānṛtam
english: It is set going by men bereft of fortune, by the poor, by unbelievers—this doctrine that decries the teaching of the Veda, falsehood wearing the semblance of truth.

sanskrit: śakyaṃ tu mauṇḍyam āsthāya bibhratātmānam ātmanā dharmacchadma samāsthāya āsituṃ na tu jīvitum
english: One may, by taking to a shaven head and maintaining oneself by oneself, putting on dharma as a disguise, manage to subsist—but not truly to live.

sanskrit: śakyaṃ punar araṇyeṣu sukham ekena jīvitum abibhratā putrapautrān devarṣīn atithīn pitṝn
english: And again, one may live easily and alone in the forests, supporting neither sons nor grandsons, neither the divine seers, nor guests, nor the ancestors.

sanskrit: neme mṛgāḥ svargajito na varāhā na pakṣiṇaḥ athaitena prakāreṇa puṇyam āhur na tāñ janāḥ
english: These deer are not winners of heaven, nor the boars, nor the birds; yet if it were by this manner of life, men would have declared them holy—and they do not.

sanskrit: yadi saṃnyāsataḥ siddhiṃ rājan kaś cid avāpnuyāt parvatāś ca drumāś caiva kṣipraṃ siddhim avāpnuyuḥ
english: If, O king, anyone could win perfection by mere renunciation, then the mountains and the trees would swiftly attain to perfection.

sanskrit: ete hi nityasaṃnyāsā dṛśyante nirupadravāḥ aparigrahavantaś ca satataṃ cātmacāriṇaḥ
english: For these are seen to be ever in renunciation, free of all affliction, owning nothing, and forever moving by their own nature alone.

sanskrit: atha ced ātmabhāgyeṣu nānyeṣāṃ siddhim aśnute tasmāt karmaiva kartavyaṃ nāsti siddhir akarmaṇaḥ
english: But if a man attains perfection by his own destiny and not by that of others, then it is action alone that must be performed; there is no perfection for the man without action.

sanskrit: audakāḥ sṛṣṭayaś caiva jantavaḥ siddhim āpnuyuḥ yeṣām ātmaiva bhartavyo nānyaḥ kaś cana vidyate
english: Then creatures of the water and the rest of created things would attain perfection—they who have only themselves to maintain and no other being whatever.

sanskrit: avekṣasva yathā svaiḥ svaiḥ karmabhir vyāpṛtaṃ jagat tasmāt karmaiva kartavyaṃ nāsti siddhir akarmaṇaḥ
english: Behold how the world is busied, each thing with its own several deeds; therefore it is action alone that must be performed; there is no perfection for the man without action.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam tāpasaiḥ saha saṃvādaṃ śakrasya bharatarṣabha
english: Arjuna said: On this very matter they tell this ancient tale, the colloquy of Śakra with certain ascetics, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: ke cid gṛhān parityajya vanam abhyagaman dvijāḥ ajātaśmaśravo mandāḥ kule jātāḥ pravavrajuḥ
english: Certain brāhmaṇas, forsaking their homes, went away to the forest—dull-witted, their beards not yet grown, born of good family, they took to the wandering life.

sanskrit: dharmo 'yam iti manvānā brahmacarye vyavasthitāḥ tyaktvā gṛhān pitṝṃś caiva tān indro 'nvakṛpāyata
english: Deeming this to be dharma, they took their stand in chastity, having abandoned their homes and their fathers; and Indra took pity upon them.

sanskrit: tān ābabhāṣe bhagavān pakṣī bhūtvā hiraṇmayaḥ suduṣkaraṃ manuṣyaiś ca yat kṛtaṃ vighasāśibhiḥ
english: The Lord, becoming a bird of gold, addressed them: "A thing most hard to do is this that men have done, men who eat the leavings of others' meals.

sanskrit: puṇyaṃ ca bata karmaiṣāṃ praśastaṃ caiva jīvitam saṃsiddhās te gatiṃ mukhyāṃ prāptā dharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Holy, indeed, is the deed of these, and praiseworthy their manner of life; perfected, devoted to dharma, they have reached the foremost goal."

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ aho batāyaṃ śakunir vighasāśān praśaṃsati asmān nūnam ayaṃ śāsti vayaṃ ca vighasāśinaḥ
english: The seers said: "Ah! this bird praises the eaters of leavings! Surely he is instructing us—for we too are eaters of leavings."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca nāhaṃ yuṣmān praśaṃsāmi paṅkadigdhān rajasvalān ucchiṣṭabhojino mandān anye vai vighasāśinaḥ
english: The bird said: "I do not praise you, smeared with mud, soiled with dust, eaters of refuse, dull of wit; quite other are the true eaters of leavings.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ idaṃ śreyaḥ param iti vayam evābhyupāsmahe śakune brūhi yac chreyo bhṛśaṃ vai śraddadhāma te
english: The seers said: "This we have honored as the supreme good. O bird, tell us what is the higher good; truly we put great faith in you."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca yadi māṃ nābhiśaṅkadhvaṃ vibhajyātmānam ātmanā tato 'haṃ vaḥ pravakṣyāmi yāthātathyaṃ hitaṃ vacaḥ
english: The bird said: "If you do not mistrust me, having tested your own selves by your own selves, then I shall declare to you a word salutary and according to the truth.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ śṛṇumas te vacas tāta panthāno viditās tava niyoge caiva dharmātman sthātum icchāma śādhi naḥ
english: The seers said: "We hearken to your word, dear one; well known to us are your ways. We wish to stand by your command, O righteous one; instruct us."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca catuṣpadāṃ gauḥ pravarā lohānāṃ kāñcanaṃ varam śabdānāṃ pravaro mantro brāhmaṇo dvipadāṃ varaḥ
english: The bird said: "Among four-footed creatures the cow is foremost; among metals gold is best; among sounds the sacred mantra is foremost; and the brāhmaṇa is the best of two-footed beings.

sanskrit: mantro 'yaṃ jātakarmādi brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate jīvato yo yathākālaṃ śmaśānanidhanād iti
english: This mantra, the rite of birth and the rest, is ordained for the brāhmaṇa, for him who lives—each in its due season—until his laying to rest in the burning-ground.

sanskrit: karmāṇi vaidikāny asya svargyaḥ panthās tv anuttamaḥ atha sarvāṇi karmāṇi mantrasiddhāni cakṣate
english: His are the Vedic rites; the path to heaven is the unsurpassed one; and they declare that all rites are made effectual by the mantra.

sanskrit: āmnāyadṛḍhavādīni tathā siddhir iheṣyate māsārdhamāsā ṛtava ādityaśaśitārakam
english: Those founded firmly upon the sacred tradition—so is fulfillment held to be attained herein. Months and half-months and seasons, the sun, the moon, and the stars,

sanskrit: īhante sarvabhūtāni tad ṛtaṃ karmasaṅginām siddhikṣetram idaṃ puṇyam ayam evāśramo mahān
english: and all beings strive on—that is the cosmic order for those bound to action. This is the holy field of fulfillment; this very order is the great stage of life.

sanskrit: atha ye karma nindanto manuṣyāḥ kāpathaṃ gatāḥ mūḍhānām arthahīnānāṃ teṣām enas tu vidyate
english: But those men who, decrying action, have gone upon the wrong road—of those deluded ones, bereft of all good, there is found only sin.

sanskrit: devavaṃśān pitṛvaṃśān brahmavaṃśāṃś ca śāśvatān saṃtyajya mūḍhā vartante tato yānty aśrutīpatham
english: Forsaking the lineages of the gods, the lineages of the ancestors, and the eternal lineages of brahman, the deluded carry on, and thereby pass onto a path not sanctioned by the scriptures.

sanskrit: etad vo 'stu tapo yuktaṃ dadānīty ṛṣicoditam tasmāt tad adhyavasatas tapasvi tapa ucyate
english: Let this be your fitting austerity—the giving prompted by the seer's word, 'I bestow.' Therefore, for one who is intent upon it, the austerity of the austere man is so named.

sanskrit: devavaṃśān pitṛvaṃśān brahmavaṃśāṃś ca śāśvatān saṃvibhajya guroś caryāṃ tad vai duṣkaram ucyate
english: Apportioning their due to the lineages of the gods, the lineages of the ancestors, and the eternal lineages of brahman, and serving one's teacher—that, truly, is called the hard thing to do.

sanskrit: devā vai duṣkaraṃ kṛtvā vibhūtiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ tasmād gārhasthyam udvoḍhuṃ duṣkaraṃ prabravīmi vaḥ
english: The very gods, by doing the hard thing, attained to supreme dominion; therefore I declare to you that to bear up the householder's life is hard to do.

sanskrit: tapaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ prajānāṃ hi mūlam etan na saṃśayaḥ kuṭumbavidhinānena yasmin sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: This is the highest austerity, and the root of all creatures—of that there is no doubt—this ordinance of the household, wherein all things have their ground.

sanskrit: etad vidus tapo viprā dvaṃdvātītā vimatsarāḥ tasmād vanaṃ madhyamaṃ ca lokeṣu tapa ucyate
english: This the brāhmaṇas, gone beyond the pairs of opposites and free of envy, have known as austerity; and so the forest life is reckoned only a middling austerity among the worlds.

sanskrit: durādharṣaṃ padaṃ caiva gacchanti vighasāśinaḥ sāyaṃprātar vibhajyānnaṃ svakuṭumbe yathāvidhi
english: And to the unassailable state go the true eaters of leavings, who at evening and at morning apportion the food within their own household according to the ordinance."
